Problem Statement | Source: HMC-PPT-20261007-01 | project scope, preprocessing_config.json | 02 | • Classify four-channel EEG into Wake, N1, N2, N3 and REM at 30-second resolution. | • Automate epoch scoring, expose evidential uncertainty, and decode recording-level stage sequences. | • Convert scored sequences into interpretable research sleep profiles. | EEG | Five-stage | classification | Sequence | decoding | Research | profile | Scope: academic engineering research; no diagnostic or clinical-validation claim.

Project Objectives | Source: HMC-PPT-20261007-01 | checkpoint_config.json, transition_config.json, biomarker_equations.md | 03 | 01  Sleep-stage classification | Predict five stages using a compact CNN–self-attention–BiLSTM evidential model. | 02  Sequence refinement | Decode stage probabilities with training-derived transitions, separately for each recording. | 03  Subject-level profiling | Compute source-defined biomarkers, compare with ground truth and apply research risk rules.

Current Research Limitations | Source: HMC-PPT-20261007-01 | final_results.json, calibration_metrics.json | 24 | • Limited cohort: 24 SN recording IDs; only four final test recordings (3,773 epochs). | • EEG-only inputs; no multimodal PSG or cross-dataset validation. | • Historical notebook test reuse limits claims of a newly blinded evaluation. | • Evidential uncertainty and reliability require stronger independent validation. | • Research biomarker definitions and thresholds are not clinically validated. | • Training hardware and final global training RNG state were not preserved.

Future Work | Source: HMC-PPT-20261007-01 | verified scope and limitations | 25 | External validation | Evaluate on independent HMC recordings and another sleep dataset. | Multimodal PSG | Test EEG + EOG + EMG with a preregistered protocol. | Generalization | Study montage, device and population changes. | Calibration | Fit any calibrator on validation data, then test once. | Clinical review | Review biomarker denominators and research thresholds with experts. | Prospective validation | Assess blinded recording-level outcomes before clinical claims.

Verified Example System Output | Source: HMC-PPT-20261007-01 | eeg_example_metadata.json, subject_risk_profiles.csv | 26 | Test recording SN009 | SE proxy: 90.01% | WASO: 14.0 min | N3 / all epochs: 23.97% | SFI: 1.18 /sleep h | Research category: Healthy | Outputs: hypnogram, epoch probabilities, uncertainty and ground-truth validation.

Conclusion | Source: HMC-PPT-20261007-01 | final_results.json, overall_metrics.json | 27 | • A compact hybrid CNN–self-attention–BiLSTM pipeline supports five-stage EEG scoring and evidential uncertainty. | • On 3,773 epochs from four test recordings, raw accuracy was 53.75%; Soft-Viterbi accuracy was 61.99%. | • All final results use one checkpoint and the same verified test epochs; SN001’s shortened input was corrected. | • Research sleep profiles are reproducible, but clinical validity and external generalization remain unestablished. | EEG → stage probabilities + uncertainty → decoded hypnogram → research sleep profile

Problem Statement | Sleep-stage analysis classifies overnight physiological recordings into five stages: Wake, N1, N2, N3 and REM. Manual scoring is time-consuming and depends on trained sleep technicians. This project automates EEG-based scoring and extends the predictions into interpretable subject-level sleep-health indicators. | Raw EEG | → | Sleep Stage Classification | → | Smoothed Hypnogram | → | Sleep Biomarkers | → | Health Risk Profile | Five-class target: Wake · N1 · N2 · N3 · REM | Scope: automated research workflow; not a clinical diagnostic system.

Project Objectives | 01 | Automatic Sleep Stage Classification | Classify every 30-second EEG epoch into Wake, N1, N2, N3 or REM. | Epoch-level prediction | 02 | Transition-Aware Sequence Refinement | Apply Soft-Viterbi decoding to reduce unrealistic rapid transitions between sleep stages. | Sequence consistency | 03 | Personalized Sleep Health Profiling | Calculate interpretable sleep indicators and assign a rule-based sleep-health risk category. | Subject-level profile | Overall Aim: EEG recording → automated sleep-health report

Current Challenges | Classification | N1 remains difficult to discriminate from neighbouring sleep stages. | Dataset | Final evaluation currently uses a limited number of test subjects. | Modality | Current system mainly relies on EEG rather than full multimodal PSG. | Verification | Some notebook outputs and dashboard values still require direct recomputation. | Profiling | Risk stratification is rule-based and requires careful clinical interpretation. | Generalization | External-dataset validation has not yet been completed. | These are research limitations and next-step priorities—not evidence of project failure.
